props.title: Five formats for your corporate event

rows.text: Booking from late November into January, the holiday party is something special for your employees and associates.
An evening built around your programming (likely including remarks, an auction, videos and walks to the stage). We work together on cues so the music flows seamlessly with the night.

Dinners where the conversation is the event. Many times we recommend a jazz duo playing low enough to add a sense of class to the ambience without demanding attention away from developing relationships.
Retreats and incentive trips in the mountain corridor, Vail through Aspen, and the Colorado foothills. We create the evening to meet the expectations of a group that flew in for it.

You know your people better than we do - and some people like to keep going after the first party ends. The hour after a conference dinner, a gala program or the holiday party’s speeches, with a DJ alone (or a DJ plus a live musician over top), a band that lets the crowd sing, or live band karaoke.

props.html: We Work around your event's program

Every great corporate evening runs on great programming. You've got remarks from leadership, maybe an an award or auction, a window of time where people need to hear each other talk. Dinner and networking are served with live music at conversation volume, and the night can get loud later, when loud is exactly the point.

image.alt: Banquet tables set for a gala under purple stage lights and screens.

props.html: The music stops while your CEO is still three steps from the microphone. Transitions are planned with the run of show.

We treat awards, auctions and videos the same way, so the music stops when it needs to and comes back in right after. If you want a louder set later in the night, live band karaoke plays the hits and hands the mic to whoever wants a song.
At a gala or fundraiser, we’ll also plan around the paddle raise and the thank-yous.

Many mountain venues have a sound limit. If yours does, let us know early and we can plan the arrangements and the instruments around it, which sounds much better than asking a band to turn down at the last minute. You can look up your town’s limit on our mountain page.

image.alt: Fireworks over a ski mountain at night, a lit town below.

props.html: We’ll work out setup with the venue ahead of time, from dock times to where the cases go during dinner. Want the details for each band size? Check out our technical page.
If your retreat is far from Denver, we’ll work out the band’s travel and lodging with you.
Have a different question? Check out our planners question list for substitutions, volume limits and more.

items.q: What does live music cost for a corporate event in Denver?
items.a: It depends on the size of the act, the hours it plays and the date. We quote each date one-by-one. What's published on our pricing page is a general market-view of what live music costs in Denver, Colorado. Send us the date, the venue and the guest count and we’ll get back to you with a recommendation and a price.

items.q: How far in advance should we book?
items.a: Whenever you're ready. Just reach out with the date and we'll check the booking calendar. If your event is coming up sooner, no worries. We can often make something great work.

items.q: Can you work with our procurement process?
items.a: Yes, we can. We can be set up as a vendor and quote against a purchase order, and we can send whatever paperwork your finance team or your venue needs. Just let us know what your process looks like.

props.title: Tell us about your event, and we'll help put the night together.
